items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I will never forget it, because I played with him until the porter swept us out.

ctx.x: Controlling, very much. And Bill kind of broke us up. And I went to live with Bill. So I started drifting away. But Win (Wingy Mannone) opened that My Cellar, and he had done some . . . Had nothing for me, and I came down there to visit. And I was just fortunate that the same night I came down, Bix came down. And I just sat there and listened.

And then, finally, this spotlight, there was one spotlight, and Sam Beers was running the place. B-e-e-r-s, he was the boss then that you might run into occasionally now in Annapolis or in Europe, the understanding man that puts the music first and the cash register second. It's a rarity, a tremendous rarity. The man that loves the arts.
